sushi in Japan just hits differently 😮‍💨👏🏻 who’s been to a conveyer belt spot in Japan?! 

📍 Kura Flagship | Tokyo, Japan 

#japan #sushi #tokyo #kura #foodvlog".
transcription: You've probably heard Sushi is better in Japan. It's true. So you know, current Irvine, right? It's solid, very quick bite, but nothing that's gonna make you text a group chat in all caps. But current Tokyo, whole differently. The conveyor belt spinning, my head spinning, and the flavors next level. The fish is so fresh, it practically way to good bite to the ocean this morning. The prices, so low, I kept checking the receipt for a hidden camera. We stacked plates higher than my ambitions, not yet actually tapped out before my wallet did. And at one point, I started feeling like I was in a sushi eating contest with myself, spoiler I want. And about those eggs, the sushi had eggs on it. And in California, you know a price for a car in like $12. I'm pretty sure I ate three cartons worth yet the grand total just $44. That's less than the market price for disappointment back home. Honestly, it felt like I was getting away with the culinary heist, except the only thing I still was a ridiculous amount of happiness and maybe not as less piece of sushi.

caption:
If you’re a sake lover, or if u wanna be, this place is a must visit 🍶

SAKE MARKET has over 100 kinds of sake, fruit wine, plum wine, shochu, and more from all over Japan for you to enjoy! They also have beer, sours, and soft drinks. It’s a self-serve style, perfect for groups. It’s such a deal for just around $28 for unlimited time of all you can drink! 🍻

There are locations in Shinjuku and Akihabara. When you reserve on Klook, use the code BLAKETOKYO for a discount! Search for “Sake All-You-Can-Drink Experience in Tokyo” or leave a comment and I can send the link ✨

#sake #japanese #japantravel #tokyo #sakelover #klookkreator #pr".
transcription: This is one of the best things to do in Japan if you're a sake lover. This place has over 100 different kinds of sake, and you can try them all because it's all you can drink here. This is how it works. You start by selecting a few cups and glasses, and then you just grab what you want and pour. The sake are divided by types, some are lighter, some are stronger, some are cloudy, and some are fruity. When you're ready for round two, just rinse out your glass and get to work. They don't serve food here, but you can bring in whatever you want. And if you reserve on clook, you can get one of these adorable sake cups to take home as a souvenir.
